source.text: בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם מ֣וּסַר אָ֑ב וְ֝לֵ֗ץ לֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע גְּעָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A wise son, [the] discipline of a father, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.

en.L: A wise son [hears his] father's discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
en.B: A wise son takes in his father's correction, but a mocker will not listen to a warning.
en.R: A wise son listens when his father corrects him. A person who makes fun of others will not listen to anyone.

decisions.choice: a wise son, a father's discipline: a verb is left out
decisions.reason: The first line has no verb; "loves" or "hears" is understood from the second line.

source.text: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־אִ֭ישׁ יֹ֣אכַל ט֑וֹב וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בֹּגְדִ֣ים חָמָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] fruit of [the] mouth of a person he eats good, but [the] appetite of [the] treacherous [is] violence.

en.L: From [the] fruit of {{gender:their|his}} mouth a person eats good, but [the] appetite of [the] treacherous [is for] violence.
en.B: People enjoy good things from the fruit of their words, but the treacherous hunger for violence.
en.R: Good words bring good things. But dishonest people are hungry to hurt others.

decisions.choice: the fruit of the mouth: as in 12:14

source.text: נֹצֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ פֹּשֵׂ֥ק שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו מְחִתָּה־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] guarding his mouth keeps his life; [one] opening wide his lips, ruin [is] his.

en.L: Whoever guards {{gender:their|his}} mouth protects {{gender:their|his}} life; whoever opens {{gender:their|his}} lips wide [comes to] ruin.
en.B: Those who watch what they say protect their lives, but those who talk carelessly come to ruin.
en.R: If you are careful about what you say, you will keep yourself safe. If you talk too much, you will ruin yourself.

decisions.choice: opens wide: gapes, blurts
decisions.reason: The verb (pasaq) means to open the lips wide, as in Ezekiel 16:25.

source.text: מִתְאַוָּ֣ה וָ֭אַיִן נַפְשׁ֣וֹ עָצֵ֑ל וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ חָרֻצִ֣ים תְּדֻשָּֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] appetite of a sluggard craves, and nothing, but [the] appetite of diligent [people] will be made fat.

en.L: The sluggard's appetite craves and [gets] nothing, but [the] appetite of [the] diligent will be richly satisfied.
en.B: The lazy want and want but get nothing, while the diligent are fully satisfied.
en.R: Lazy people want things, but they never get them. People who work hard get all they need.

decisions.choice: made fat: richly satisfied
decisions.reason: As in 11:25.

source.text: דְּבַר־שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א צַדִּ֑יק וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע יַבְאִ֥ישׁ וְיַחְפִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: A word of falsehood a righteous [person] hates, but a wicked [person] acts odiously and shamefully.

en.L: [The] righteous hates a false word, but [the] wicked brings stench and shame.
en.B: The righteous hate lies, but the wicked bring disgust and disgrace.
en.R: Good people hate lies. But evil people do disgusting and shameful things.

decisions.choice: brings stench and shame: acts disgracefully
decisions.reason: The first verb (hibish) is related to the word for a bad smell (Genesis 34:30); the wicked make themselves odious.

source.text: צְ֭דָקָה תִּצֹּ֣ר תָּם־דָּ֑רֶךְ וְ֝רִשְׁעָ֗ה תְּסַלֵּ֥ף חַטָּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: Righteousness guards [the] integrity of way, but wickedness overthrows sin.

en.L: Righteousness guards [the one whose] way [is] blameless, but wickedness overthrows [the] sinner.
en.B: Righteousness protects the person of integrity, but wickedness brings down the sinner.
en.R: Doing right protects honest people. But evil destroys sinners.

decisions.choice: integrity ... sin: abstract nouns for people
decisions.reason: "Integrity of way" and "sin" stand for the person of integrity and the sinner.

source.text: יֵ֣שׁ מִ֭תְעַשֵּׁר וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל מִ֝תְרוֹשֵׁ֗שׁ וְה֣וֹן רָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: There is [one] making himself rich, and nothing at all; [one] making himself poor, and wealth much.

en.L: There is one who makes {{gender:themselves|himself}} rich yet has nothing; one who makes {{gender:themselves|himself}} poor yet [has] great wealth.
en.B: Some pretend to be rich but have nothing; others pretend to be poor but have great wealth.
en.R: Some people act rich but have nothing. Other people act poor but are really rich.

decisions.choice: makes himself rich: pretends to be
alternatives: becomes rich (in money but poor in what matters)
decisions.reason: The reflexive verbs may mean pretending, or real gain and loss: one gets rich and has nothing worth having; another gives away and is rich (11:24).

source.text: כֹּ֣פֶר נֶֽפֶשׁ־אִ֣ישׁ עָשְׁר֑וֹ וְ֝רָ֗שׁ לֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע גְּעָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] ransom of [the] life of a person [is] his wealth, but a poor [person] does not hear a threat.

en.L: A person's riches [are the] ransom for {{gender:their|his}} life, but [the] poor does not hear a threat.
en.B: The rich may have to pay a ransom for their lives, but the poor never even hear a threat.
en.R: Rich people may have to pay money to save their lives. But no one bothers to threaten the poor.

decisions.choice: ransom ... threat: wealth draws danger
decisions.reason: Wealth can buy a life back from kidnappers, but it also makes a person a target. No one threatens the poor; they have nothing to take.

source.text: אוֹר־צַדִּיקִ֥ים יִשְׂמָ֑ח וְנֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] light of righteous [people] rejoices, but [the] lamp of wicked [people] goes out.

en.L: [The] light of [the] righteous shines brightly, but [the] lamp of [the] wicked goes out.
en.B: The light of the righteous burns bright, but the wicked have a lamp that will be snuffed out.
en.R: The lives of good people are like a bright light. The lives of evil people are like a lamp that goes out.

decisions.choice: rejoices: shines brightly; goes out: dies
decisions.reason: A lamp left burning was a sign of life in a house; its going out, of death and ruin (20:20; 24:20; Job 18:5–6).

source.text: רַק־בְּ֭זָדוֹן יִתֵּ֣ן מַצָּ֑ה וְאֶת־נ֖וֹעָצִ֣ים חָכְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Only with pride [one] gives strife, but with those taking advice [is] wisdom.

en.L: By pride comes only strife, but with those who take advice [is] wisdom.
en.B: Arrogance only stirs up fights, but those who take advice are wise.
en.R: Pride causes nothing but fights. Wise people listen to advice.

decisions.choice: pride: presumption (11:2)
decisions.reason: As in 11:2.

source.text: ה֭וֹן מֵהֶ֣בֶל יִמְעָ֑ט וְקֹבֵ֖ץ עַל־יָ֣ד יַרְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Wealth from vapor will diminish, but [one] gathering by hand will increase.

en.L: Wealth [gained] from nothing will dwindle, but whoever gathers little by little will increase [it].
en.B: Money that comes easily soon dwindles, but whoever gathers it bit by bit makes it grow.
en.R: Money that comes quickly soon disappears. But money that is saved little by little grows.

decisions.choice: from nothing: easily or dishonestly gained
decisions.reason: The word (hebel) is vapor, nothing (Ecclesiastes 1:2). The ancient Greek reads "wealth gained in haste" (compare 20:21; 28:20).

decisions.choice: by hand: little by little
decisions.reason: "On hand" means gradually, by one's own work.

source.text: תּוֹחֶ֣לֶת מְ֭מֻשָּׁכָה מַחֲלָה־לֵ֑ב וְעֵ֥ץ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תַּאֲוָ֥ה בָאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Hope drawn out makes sick [the] heart, but a tree of life [is] a desire coming.

en.L: Hope delayed makes [the] heart sick, but a desire fulfilled [is] a tree of life.
en.B: When hope keeps being put off, the heart grows sick, but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.
en.R: Waiting a long time for something you hope for can make you sad. But getting what you longed for brings you new life.

decisions.choice: a tree of life: as in 3:18

source.text: בָּ֣ז לְ֭דָבָר יֵחָ֣בֶל ל֑וֹ וִירֵ֥א מִ֝צְוָ֗ה ה֣וּא יְשֻׁלָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] despising a word will be in pledge to it, but [one] fearing a command, he will be rewarded.

en.L: Whoever despises [the] word will pay for it, but whoever fears [the] command will be rewarded.
en.B: Whoever scorns instruction will pay the price, but whoever respects a command will be rewarded.
en.R: If you ignore good teaching, you will suffer for it. If you obey commands, you will be rewarded.

decisions.choice: the word ... the command: instruction, perhaps God's
decisions.reason: "The word" and "the command" may be a parent's teaching or God's (Deuteronomy 30:14).

decisions.choice: pay for it: be held as a pledge, owe a debt
decisions.reason: The verb (habal) may mean to be taken in pledge, as for a debt, or to be ruined.

source.text: תּוֹרַ֣ת חָ֭כָם מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] teaching of a wise [person] [is] a fountain of life, to turn aside from snares of death.

en.L: [The] teaching of [the] wise [is] a fountain of life, to turn [one] aside from [the] snares of death.
en.B: What the wise teach is a spring of life, steering people away from the traps of death.
en.R: The teaching of wise people gives life. It helps people stay away from things that lead to death.

decisions.choice: a fountain of life: as in 10:11
decisions.reason: The same saying is made of the fear of the LORD in 14:27.

source.text: שֵֽׂכֶל־ט֭וֹב יִתֶּן־חֵ֑ן וְדֶ֖רֶךְ בֹּגְדִ֣ים אֵיתָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Good insight gives favor, but [the] way of [the] treacherous [is] enduring.

en.L: Good sense wins favor, but [the] way of [the] treacherous [is] hard.
en.B: Good sense wins goodwill, but the way of the treacherous is rough going.
en.R: People like those who have good sense. But dishonest people have a hard life.

decisions.choice: hard: rough, unyielding
decisions.reason: The word (etan) usually means lasting or perennial (a stream that never dries up). Here, set against "favor", it seems to mean hard, like stony ground. The ancient Greek reads "leads to ruin".

source.text: כָּל־עָ֭רוּם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה בְדָ֑עַת וּ֝כְסִ֗יל יִפְרֹ֥שׂ אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: Every prudent [person] acts with knowledge, but a fool spreads out folly.

en.L: Every prudent [person] acts with knowledge, but a fool spreads out folly.
en.B: The prudent act with knowledge, but fools put their folly on display.
en.R: Wise people think before they act. Fools show everyone how foolish they are.

decisions.choice: spreads out: displays, like a merchant spreading out goods
decisions.reason: The verb (paras) is used of spreading out a garment or wares.

source.text: מַלְאָ֣ךְ רָ֭שָׁע יִפֹּ֣ל בְּרָ֑ע וְצִ֖יר אֱמוּנִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy [is] healing.

en.L: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy [brings] healing.
en.B: An unreliable messenger lands in trouble, but a trustworthy envoy brings healing.
en.R: A dishonest messenger causes trouble. A messenger you can trust helps make things better.

decisions.choice: messenger ... envoy: a person sent to carry word
decisions.reason: Messages went by personal messenger, who could ruin or heal relations between people (25:13; 26:6).

source.text: רֵ֣ישׁ וְ֭קָלוֹן פּוֹרֵ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר וְשׁוֹמֵ֖ר תּוֹכַ֣חַת יְכֻבָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Poverty and shame [to one] ignoring discipline, but [one] keeping correction is honored.

en.L: Poverty and shame [come to] whoever ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
en.B: Poverty and disgrace come to the one who ignores discipline, but whoever accepts correction is honored.
en.R: People who will not accept correction end up poor and ashamed. People who learn from correction are respected.

decisions.choice: ignores: lets go, neglects
decisions.reason: The verb (para) of 1:25 and 8:33.

source.text: תַּאֲוָ֣ה נִ֭הְיָה תֶּעֱרַ֣ב לְנָ֑פֶשׁ וְתוֹעֲבַ֥ת כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: A desire fulfilled is sweet to [the] soul, but an abomination of fools [is] turning from evil.

en.L: A desire fulfilled [is] sweet to [the] soul, but turning from evil [is] an abomination to fools.
en.B: A wish come true is sweet to the soul, but fools hate to turn away from evil.
en.R: It feels good to get what you hope for. But fools hate to stop doing evil.

decisions.choice: a desire fulfilled ... turning from evil: what fools will not give up
decisions.reason: The two lines are loosely joined. Fools want their desires so much they will not turn from evil to reach better ones.

source.text: הוֹלֵ֣ךְאֶת־חֲכָמִ֣ים יֶחְכָּ֑ם וְרֹעֶ֖ה כְסִילִ֣ים יֵרֽוֹעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] walking with wise [people] will become wise, but [one] associating with fools will be harmed.

en.L: Whoever walks with [the] wise will become wise, but whoever keeps company with fools will be harmed.
en.B: Spend time with the wise and you will grow wise; keep company with fools and you will get hurt.
en.R: If you spend time with wise people, you will become wise. If you spend time with fools, you will get into trouble.

decisions.choice: walks ... will become wise, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: walk with the wise and become wise (commands, the written form)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read two commands; the reading the scribes marked (qere) gives a statement. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: keeps company ... will be harmed: wordplay
decisions.reason: "Keep company" (roeh) and "be harmed" (yeroa) sound alike.

source.text: חַ֭טָּאִים תְּרַדֵּ֣ף רָעָ֑ה וְאֶת־צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים יְשַׁלֶּם־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: Sinners, calamity pursues, but righteous [people], it repays good.

en.L: Disaster pursues sinners, but [the] righteous are repaid [with] good.
en.B: Trouble chases sinners, but the righteous are rewarded with good things.
en.R: Trouble follows sinners. But good people are rewarded with good things.

decisions.choice: repaid with good: by God
decisions.reason: The subject of "repay" may be "good" itself or God, unnamed.

source.text: ט֗וֹב יַנְחִ֥יל בְּנֵֽי־בָנִ֑ים וְצָפ֥וּן לַ֝צַּדִּ֗יק חֵ֣יל חוֹטֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: A good [person] leaves an inheritance [to] children of children, but stored up for [the] righteous [is the] wealth of a sinner.

en.L: A good [person] leaves an inheritance to {{gender:grandchildren|sons' sons}}, but a sinner's wealth [is] stored up for [the] righteous.
en.B: A good person leaves an inheritance to their grandchildren, but the wealth of a sinner ends up with the righteous.
en.R: Good people leave money for their grandchildren. But the riches of sinners will end up with good people.

decisions.choice: children of children: grandchildren
decisions.reason: "Sons of sons" means descendants, daughters as well as sons (17:6).

source.text: רָב־אֹ֭כֶל נִ֣יר רָאשִׁ֑ים וְיֵ֥שׁ נִ֝סְפֶּ֗ה בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: Much food [is in the] fallow ground of [the] poor, but there is [what is] swept away by lack of justice.

en.L: [The] unplowed ground of [the] poor [yields] much food, but it is swept away through injustice.
en.B: The fields of the poor may produce plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it away.
en.R: Poor people's fields may grow plenty of food. But unfair people can take it all away.

decisions.choice: the poor's harvest, lost to injustice
alternatives: some perish for lack of judgment
decisions.reason: The verse is hard. It most likely says that the poor could have enough if they were not robbed by injustice. The ancient Greek is quite different.

source.text: חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ שִׁ֭בְטוֹ שׂוֹנֵ֣א בְנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֹהֲב֗וֹ שִֽׁחֲר֥וֹ מוּסָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] holding back his rod hates his son, but [one] loving him seeks him [with] discipline.

en.L: Whoever holds back {{gender:their|his}} rod hates {{gender:their|his}} son, but whoever loves him is diligent [to] discipline him.
en.B: Whoever holds back the rod hates their son, but the one who loves him is quick to discipline him.
en.R: If you do not discipline your son, you do not really love him. If you love him, you will correct him when he needs it.

decisions.choice: the rod: physical discipline
decisions.reason: The rod was the usual means of correcting a child in the ancient world (22:15; 23:13–14; 29:15). The point of the saying is that love corrects; the means belongs to its time and must be read in the light of all Scripture says about love and justice.

decisions.choice: is diligent to discipline: seeks him early with discipline
decisions.reason: The verb (shahar) of 1:28 and 8:17: eager, early seeking.

source.text: צַדִּ֗יק אֹ֭כֵל לְשֹׂ֣בַע נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּבֶ֖טֶן רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֶּחְסָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: A righteous [person] eats to [the] satisfying of his appetite, but [the] belly of wicked [people] lacks.

en.L: [The] righteous eats to {{gender:their|his}} heart's content, but [the] belly of [the] wicked goes hungry.
en.B: The righteous have enough to eat, but the stomachs of the wicked go empty.
en.R: Good people have all the food they need. But evil people go hungry.

decisions.choice: eats ... goes hungry: as in 10:3
